Base directory for this skill: /ux/run/work/.claude/skills/metais

# metais

A `.metais` file is a METAIS package: a document template. It declares
the inputs a document needs, each with a JSON Schema and a guide to what
it means, and renders the document from them. The `metais` command reads
it, checks inputs against it and renders it.

## Rules

- **Read a package with `metais`, in place.** Never unzip it, never read
  its raw bytes, never `cat` its README. Every command below takes the
  `.metais` file, or a source directory, as it is.
- **Never invent facts for a real document.** The inputs come from the
  person or from the sources they name. A value nobody supplied is asked
  for, not guessed, and not filled with a placeholder.
- **Fictional data only when the person asks for it** ("example data",
  "sample", "demo", "a preview"). Then generate it with
  `metais render <package> --sample` or `metais sample`; never copy a
  package's examples, and never hand-write placeholder values. An example
  is the author's illustration of the inputs, not the person's data.
- **Follow `next`.** Every command ends with the commands to run next
  (`Next:` in text, `next` in JSON). `<package>`, `<dir>` and `<data dir>`
  there are placeholders for your own paths.

## Filling in and rendering a package

1. `metais inspect report.metais` — what the package is, its guide, every
   input (with the file name it takes in a data directory, such as
   `status.json`), every output, and "Read next". Read all of it. If the
   guide was cut, `metais inspect report.metais --guide`.
2. Run what "Read next" lists, in order:
   - `metais read report.metais <entry>` for each input's meaning document;
   - `metais grep report.metais <pattern> references/` for the references.
3. `metais schema report.metais <input> --fields` — the fields of one
   input, one line each: its pointer (as `--set` takes it), its type,
   `required` or `optional`, its constraints and its title. Read it whole.
   A line that ends `when …` applies only under that condition, such as a
   field another field's value makes required. With no input it lists
   every input's fields; with `--json` they are `result.fields`. Only
   after it, for a field's description, read the whole schema:
   `metais schema report.metais <input>`, or write it to a file with
   `> <input>.schema.json`. Never dig fields out of its `$defs`: the
   listing has already followed every `$ref`.
4. Write a data directory: one file per input, named as `inspect` shows
   (`<input>.json`, `<input>.csv`, …), or one directory per collection
   input. `metais help inputs` explains `--set` and `--inputs-json`, which
   supply values on the command line instead.
5. `metais validate report.metais --data <data dir>` — every finding at
   once. Fix them all and run it again until it is clean.
6. `metais render report.metais --data <data dir> --out <new dir>` — the
   document. `--out` must be a new or empty directory; `--dry-run` lists
   what it would write.

**Fictional data, when asked for:**
`metais render report.metais --sample --out <new dir>` renders an example
of the document from generated data, in one step.
`metais sample report.metais --out <data dir>` writes valid generated data
to start from (`--seed <n>` varies it); then `validate` and `render` as
above. Say in your answer that the data is fictional. Never use generated
data for a real document.

## Writing a package

1. `metais init <dir> --minimal` — a new source directory with one input
   and one template to replace; without `--minimal`, a greeting with an
   example to learn from. Add `--html` for an HTML output: it declares
   `escape: html`, and its template writes data into a `<script>` with
   `json_script`, never `json`.
2. Edit `metais.yaml`, `inputs/`, `templates/` and `examples/`.
   `metais help manifest` gives every field of `metais.yaml` with an
   example; `metais help templates` gives the template language, every
   filter, and escaping, a URL component's `url_encode` included. Preview
   with `metais render <dir> --sample --out <preview dir>`.
3. `metais check <dir>` — every defect, without data.
4. `metais test <dir>` — renders each example and compares it with its
   `expected/` outputs; `metais test <dir> --update` records them.
5. `metais pack <dir>` — check, test, and write `<name>-<version>.metais`.

To change a packed package: `metais unpack report.metais --out <dir>`,
edit, then `check`, `test` and `pack`.

## Machine output

`--json` on any command prints exactly one JSON document on standard
output: `{"format", "ok", "findings", "summary", "result", "next"}`.
`ok` is false when any finding is an error; each finding has a `code`,
a `message` and a `hint`. `metais help json` lists every format.

## When stuck

- `metais help` — the commands and both paths.
- `metais help <command>` — a command's operands, flags, refusals and
  examples.
- `metais help inputs` — supplying inputs, and which source wins.
- `metais help templates` and `metais help manifest` — writing templates
  and `metais.yaml`.
- `metais help refusals <command>` — every code a command can report, with
  the next step.
- A finding's `hint` says what to do; its code is stable.

This skill was installed by `metais skill`. If `metais version` is newer
than the version in the last line, `metais skill --dry-run` says whether to
refresh it.

content.content: metais help manifest — Every field of metais.yaml, inputs and outputs included. Examples: A complete metais.yaml: a package with two inputs, one of which may be supplied as CSV, rendered to Markdown and to an HTML page that escapes its values. metais: "1.0" name: org.example.release-notes version: "1.2.0" title: Release notes description: Release notes for one product release, in Markdown and HTML. guide: |- Supply the release first, then its changes. Read inputs/changes.md for what a good change says. authors: - name: Example Docs Team email: docs@example.org url: https://example.org/docs license: Apache-2.0 homepage: https://example.org/release-notes inputs: - name: release title: The release schema: inputs/release.schema.json - name: changes title: The changes in the release description: One change per row, newest first. schema: inputs/changes.schema.json meaning: inputs/changes.md forms: [json, yaml, csv] csv: delimiter: ";" outputs: - id: notes template: notes.md.liquid - id: page template: page.html.liquid path: "{{ inputs.release.version }}/index.html" escape: html The same package's outputs could instead write one page per change with for_each, and a zip holding a template, an asset and a mirror: outputs: - id: change_pages template: change.md.liquid for_each: inputs.changes when: item.public path: "changes/{{ item.id }}.md" - id: bundle path: "release-{{ inputs.release.version }}.zip" container: format: zip entries: - template: notes.md.liquid path: README.md first: true - asset: logo.png path: images/logo.png stored: true - mirror: site path: site escape: html The manifest's top level: metais Required. The METAIS specification version the package targets, as a quoted string: unquoted, 1.0 is the number 1. A tool processes the package under exactly that version's rules. Example: metais: "1.0" name Required. The package's name: segments of lower-case ASCII letters and digits, single hyphens between them, joined by dots. A segment is at most 63 characters and the name at most 128, and the first segment is not a Windows device name (con, prn, aux, nul, com0 to com9, lpt0 to lpt9). A package published beyond its author should begin with a domain its publisher controls, reversed. Example: name: org.example.release-notes version Required. The package's own version, a Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 version of at most 128 characters, without a leading v and quoted. Pre-release and build metadata are allowed. Example: version: "1.2.0-rc.1" title Required. What the package is, as a person names it: one line of 1 to 200 characters. Example: title: Release notes description Required. What the package produces, in a sentence or a short paragraph of 1 to 1000 characters, displayed verbatim. Example: description: Release notes for one product release. guide Required. The guide for suppliers, in CommonMark, of 1 to 16384 characters: what the package is for, how its inputs relate, the order to gather them in, and where to read further. It may not end with a line break, so write a block as guide: |- rather than guide: |. Example: guide: Supply the release first, then its changes. authors Optional. The package's authors, 1 to 64 people or organizations, each an object with the fields under authors[]. Example: authors: [{name: Example Docs Team}] license Optional. The terms of the package's own content, an SPDX license expression of 1 to 512 characters with AND, OR and WITH in upper case. Identifiers are not checked against the SPDX License List. Example: license: Apache-2.0 OR MIT homepage Optional. The package's home page, an absolute https or http URI of at most 2048 characters, with a host, no user information and no fragment. No command ever fetches it. Example: homepage: https://example.org/release-notes inputs Required. The inputs the package takes, in the order a supplier meets them, each an object with the fields under inputs[]. It may be empty. Example: inputs: [] input_constraints Optional. The package path, under inputs/ and ending .json, .yaml or .yml, of a schema evaluated against the object holding every input, for rules that relate one input to another. Example: input_constraints: inputs/constraints.schema.json outputs Required. The output declarations, at least one, in the order they are planned, each with the fields under outputs[]. Example: outputs: [{id: notes, template: notes.md.liquid}] Each author, authors[]: authors[].name Required. The person or organization: one line of 1 to 200 characters. Example: name: Ada Lovelace authors[].email Optional. An email address of 3 to 254 characters, with exactly one @ and no space. It is not validated further, and no command sends mail. Example: email: ada@example.org authors[].url Optional. The author's web page, an absolute https or http URI with a host and no user information, as homepage. Example: url: https://example.org/ada Each input, inputs[] (spec chapter 5): inputs[].name Required. The input's name, unique among the inputs: a lower-case letter, then up to 63 lower-case letters, digits and underscores, and none of Liquid's reserved words blank, empty, false, first, last, nil, null, size and true. A template reads the input as inputs., a data directory's file for it is named after it, and it is the first token of a --set pointer. Example: name: changes inputs[].title Required. What the input is, in brief: one line of 1 to 200 characters. Example: title: The changes in the release inputs[].description Optional. What the input means, as plain text, line breaks allowed. Example: description: One change per row, newest first. inputs[].schema Required. The package path, under inputs/, of the input's JSON Schema file, ending .json, .yaml or .yml. Example: schema: inputs/changes.schema.json inputs[].meaning Optional. The package path, under inputs/, of a CommonMark document ending .md that says what the data is for and what good data looks like. No tool interprets it. Example: meaning: inputs/changes.md inputs[].forms Optional. The file forms the input may be supplied in, each at most once, of json, yaml, csv, text and markdown. Default: json and yaml. Example: forms: [json, yaml, csv] inputs[].csv Optional, and allowed only when forms holds csv. How a CSV file of the input is read: an object whose one member is delimiter. Example: csv: {delimiter: ";"} inputs[].csv.delimiter Required in csv. The character that separates fields: a comma, a semicolon, a vertical bar or a tab. Example: delimiter: "\t" inputs[].collection Optional. true for a collection: an array of items, supplied as a directory of item files. Default false. Example: collection: true inputs[].required Optional. false for an input a supplier may leave out. Default true. Example: required: false Each output declaration, outputs[] (spec chapters 9 and 10): A declaration takes exactly one form, named by the one source key it carries: template, asset, mirror or container. Each field below names the forms that take it, and a form refuses any other field. outputs[].id Every form. Required at the top level and optional on a container entry. The declaration's identifier: a lower-case letter, then up to 63 lower-case letters, digits and underscores, unique among the top-level declarations, and an entry's among its container's entries. Example: id: change_pages outputs[].template The template form's source key: the template's path relative to 242: json_script json for a " | json_script }} 289- gives 290- 291- 292-'metais help manifest' gives the fields of metais.yaml; spec chapters 7, 8 and 9 293-give the environment, the filters and tags, and the outputs in full.

/ux/run/work/number-chart
metais test — Render every example of a package and compare it with the outputs
it should produce.

Usage:
  metais test [<package>] [--example <name>]... [--update [--dry-run]]
              [--limit <name>=<value>]... [--json]

Examples:
  metais test
      Tests every example of the source directory in the working directory.
  metais test report-1.0.0.metais --example basic
      Tests the example basic of a packed package.
  metais test --update --dry-run
      Lists what --update would write into and remove from each example's
      expected/.
  metais test --json
      Prints every finding and each example's result as one metais.test/1
      document.

The package is a source directory, the current directory when omitted, or a
packed package file, whose examples are read in place. The package is opened and
verified whole, and every template is parsed; an error there is reported and no
example runs.

An example is a directory under examples/: inputs/ is a data directory, read as
--data reads one; expected/ is the output directory a render should write;
example.yaml may give a title, a description, and now, the render time. Every
example runs, or each one --example names, in byte order of name, whatever
another found. Its inputs are validated, with findings located in
examples/<name>/inputs/; if they are valid it is rendered in memory as metais
render renders, with now from example.yaml or none, and nothing else of the
host. The package digest a template sees, and the provenance tag's
package_digest, are sha256: and 64 zeros, and the provenance tool is test, so an
expected output records nothing that changes with the package or the tool.

When expected/ exists, its files are compared with the render's by path, byte
for byte but for a container; directories are ignored. A file the render did not
write is example.output_missing, one it wrote that expected/ lacks is
example.output_unexpected, and different content is example.output_differs: for
text, a unified diff, of at most 40 lines here and 16 KiB in --json; for a
binary file, the first differing byte and both sizes and digests. Its cause
names the first likely explanation that applies: line endings, one final
newline, a byte order mark, or trailing whitespace.

A container output is compared by its entries, not its zip's bytes: their names
in order, each entry's uncompressed content, and the method of each entry
declared stored: true and of a profile's mimetype; any other entry's method is
the encoder's choice and is not compared. The expected container is read as a
packed package is, with its bounds and profile, but in its entries' own order,
and one that does not read is example.expected_unreadable. An entry expected and
not written is example.entry_missing, one written and not expected
example.entry_unexpected, entries in another order example.entry_order, at the
first index where they differ, a stored entry the expected container deflates
example.entry_method, and different content example.output_differs, located at
<output>!<entry>; a container entry is compared by its own entries. An example
without expected/ is rendered and not compared.

--update, on a source directory only, makes each selected example's expected/
exactly its render: every file that is missing or differs is written, through a
staging directory inside expected/, and every file there the render no longer

expected output records nothing that changes with the package or the tool.

When expected/ exists, its files are compared with the render's by path, byte
for byte but for a container; directories are ignored. A file the render did not
write is example.output_missing, one it wrote that expected/ lacks is
example.output_unexpected, and different content is example.output_differs: for
text, a unified diff, of at most 40 lines here and 16 KiB in --json; for a
binary file, the first differing byte and both sizes and digests. Its cause
names the first likely explanation that applies: line endings, one final
newline, a byte order mark, or trailing whitespace.

A container output is compared by its entries, not its zip's bytes: their names
in order, each entry's uncompressed content, and the method of each entry
declared stored: true and of a profile's mimetype; any other entry's method is
the encoder's choice and is not compared. The expected container is read as a
packed package is, with its bounds and profile, but in its entries' own order,
and one that does not read is example.expected_unreadable. An entry expected and
not written is example.entry_missing, one written and not expected
example.entry_unexpected, entries in another order example.entry_order, at the
first index where they differ, a stored entry the expected container deflates
example.entry_method, and different content example.output_differs, located at
<output>!<entry>; a container entry is compared by its own entries. An example
without expected/ is rendered and not compared.

content.text: I've built the package as `number-chart-0.1.0.metais`, from the source directory `number-chart/`. `metais check` reports no problems, the example render passes `metais test`, and `metais pack` succeeded. **What it takes.** One input, `data`, supplied as `data.json` or `data.yaml`: - `title` (required): the page heading. - `values` (required): the numbers to chart, from 1 to 1000 of them, in left-to-right order. - `unit` (optional): a short unit such as `ms` or `°C`, shown on the axis and in each bar's tooltip. **What it produces.** A single `index.html` page. The template writes the numbers straight into the page's script, so the example renders as: ```js const values = [3.5,-1.2,0,4.8,2.1,-3.4,1.7]; const unit = "°C"; ``` A small script then draws a bar chart from that array as an SVG. Bars are measured from zero, so negative numbers point down. The chart also has: - evenly spaced y-axis gridlines and labels - numbered x-axis labels, thinned out when there are many bars - a tooltip on each bar - light and dark colour schemes - an accessible label for screen readers **Safety.** Text is HTML-escaped in the title and heading. Values reach the script through `json_script`, so they can't break out of the `x` as the title and `` as the unit: both came out escaped. **Testing.** I ran the chart script against a stand-in for the browser page, not in a real browser. The bar heights and axis labels it produced were correct, including for zero and negative values. I haven't seen the page displayed in a browser. To chart your own numbers: ``` metais render number-chart-0.1.0.metais --data --out ``` The source directory holds: - `metais.yaml` - `inputs/data.schema.json` - `inputs/data.md`, a guide to the input - `templates/page.html.liquid` - one test example, `examples/basic/` (seven daily temperature changes), with its saved output
